_readme: Hand-edited. The indexer NEVER writes this file.
After editing run: npm run index-faces:recluster  (seconds — detection is cached)
Applied in order: ignoreFaces/ignorePhotos -> split -> merge -> people attributes.
Person ids are stable across re-runs. See face-index/review.json for every
detected person, their photo count and the borderline pairs worth deciding on.

_schema.people: { "p-0001": { name, featured, order, cover, hidden, note } }
_schema.merge: [["p-0001","p-0003"]] — first id is canonical, the rest are absorbed

_mergeHistoryNote: The 78-photo-era merge entries (old p-0003/p-0004/.../p-0029) were removed
from this list on 2026-08-12: after re-clustering the full 875-photo set,
none of those ids exist anymore (fresh clustering + tier-2 identity
consolidation reshaped everything). The 4 people hidden from that era
(old p-0025-p-0028) are also gone as independent entities for the same
reason — nothing currently needs hiding under those old ids.
Below are duplicate-identity fragments found in the 875-photo set that
identity consolidation (tools/face-index/lib/identity-consolidation.mjs)
did NOT auto-merge because their centroid distance landed in the
conservative gray-zone (0.36-0.44) rather than clearing the 0.36 auto-merge
bar — see face-index/review.json 'possibleDuplicateIdentities' for the
full list with distances. Each entry below was independently verified by
visually comparing face crops before merging, per the instruction not to
merge on guest-number alone.
Nadav: p-0097 (extreme side profile), p-0159 (side profile, laughing),
p-0213 (sunglasses — same failure mode as the original p-0003 case: dark
glasses destroy the eye region the descriptor relies on) all visually
confirmed as Nadav. p-0239 and p-0250 were NOT merged — both crops show two
men embracing cheek-to-cheek and it isn't possible to confirm by eye which
face is the detected one; left for manual review in overrides if you can
confirm from the original photos.
visually confirmed as Sharon (her distinctive curly auburn hair is clearly
visible in each crop) despite elevated embedding distance — these are
mostly candid shots under coloured party lighting or with motion blur,
which measurably degrades embedding quality without changing what a human
eye can plainly see. p-0279 and p-0199 were NOT merged: p-0279's crop is
mostly obscured by hair/shadow and too uncertain to confirm; p-0199's faces
landed in a different existing cluster (p-0086) with a similar-looking
hairstyle rather than with Sharon — worth a manual look if you recognise
p-0086. p-0123 and p-0269 (originally on the list) were checked and their
faces are NOT Sharon by any measure (embedding distance 0.6+, clearly a
different person) — they were correctly left unmerged, now sitting unsorted.
